terms.gloss: see to it that, take care that
terms.grammar: imperative of cūrāre with ut and the subjunctive; future cūrābō ut, I’ll see to it that
evidence: Cic. Att. 3.7.3: vidēre tē cupiō. cūrā ut valeās.
Traupman p. 107: I’ll see to it that …, cūrābō ut (+ subj.)
terms.comment: The letter-writer’s cūrā ut valeās is “look after yourself”: literally “see to it that you are well”.

terms.grammar: future imperative of facere with ut (utī) and the subjunctive
evidence: Cato Agr. 5.6: arātra vōmerēsque facitō utī bonōs habeās
Plaut. Mil. 4.4.1: praecepta facitō ut meminerīs (Lewis & Short s.v. meminī)
Traupman p. 107: see that you do it, facitō ut faciās
terms.comment: The future imperative gives a standing instruction: Cato’s farm manual is full of facitō.

phrases.latin: cūrā ut valeās et nōs amēs et tibi persuādeās tē ā mē frāternē amārī
phrases.english: look after yourself, love us, and be sure that I love you like a brother

sources: Lewis & Short: curo · Lewis & Short: facio
